_source: Morning_Report_Scorecard.pdf — the printed strike-out card. Sixteen items in two columns plus four automatic fails. The web scorecard and the CLI both read this file; do not restate the items anywhere else.
_codes_note: `code` is the identifier the printed rubric and the CLI share (A1-A7, B1-B9, F1-F4). `scored_from` says where a verdict can legitimately come from: manifest, transcript, timing, derived, or human-only. An item marked human is never sent to a model.
_derived_note: `derived` names a key in the board archive's derived block. Those items arrive pre-ticked and marked, and the facilitator can override any of them. Six are the ones the spec lists; test_named and any_struck are here on the same footing because they are board fields too, not judgements.
title: Strike it out
lede: Cross each one off as it happens. What is left standing at 0:25 is the feedback — no debrief required.
footer: One per session. If the same box survives four weeks running, that is the thing to teach.

items.text: De-identified — no MRN, no dates, no burned-in IDs
items.evidence: Facilitator attestation. Also flag if the transcript itself contains an MRN or date-of-service pattern.
An objective stated in the first 90 seconds. Exactly one; two or more is a fail.
The first substantive presenter turn leads with the clinical situation, not a recitation of past history, medications or family history.

items.text: History and exam in one block — no labs yet
items.evidence: No lab value, imaging result or micro result appears before the first PGY-1 turn.

items.text: Stopped talking and let the silence run
items.evidence: Not scorable from a transcript. Always null, always human.

items.text: Reveal named what was missed, and why
items.evidence: After the reveal the presenter names something the team got wrong or late AND gives a reason. Naming the diagnosis alone does not count.
One summarising sentence from the PGY-1 with semantic qualifiers — age, tempo, key features. A list of findings is not a problem representation.

items.text: Three to four diagnoses, each with a reason
items.evidence: Three or four distinct entity-level diagnoses from the PGY-1, each with a rationale. Categories such as 'infectious' are not items. Fewer than three or more than four is a fail.
The PGY-1 explicitly labels one diagnosis as the can't-miss, must-not-miss or worst case.
No non-PGY-1 turn longer than about five words between the start and end of the first pass, other than the facilitator calling the clock.

items.text: A framework named before the list
items.evidence: The senior names an organising scheme — anatomic level or layer, physiologic, pre/intra/post, mechanism, age, tempo, triage — BEFORE enumerating diagnoses. Order matters.

items.text: Something struck off, with the reason beside it
items.evidence: A named diagnosis is ruled out AND the feature that argues against it is stated. Ruling out without a reason does not count.
A specific test is named as the thing that separates the top candidates, with what a positive and a negative would each mean.

items.text: Confidence stated, and what would change my mind
items.evidence: A working diagnosis with a confidence expression AND an explicit falsifying condition. Both halves are required.

automatic_fails_title: It did not hit the standard if any of these are true

automatic_fails.text: The diagnosis came out before the second pass finished
automatic_fails.evidence: The diagnosis was stated before the second pass finished.
The last cue timestamp is past 25:00.

automatic_fails.text: Nothing on the board ever got crossed off
automatic_fails.evidence: True when struck_reason (B6) is false — nothing was ever crossed off.
